lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 14: StatefulSets, stable names and a disk per Pod
lesson.description: Run stateful apps with StatefulSets: stable Pod names and DNS, a headless Service, one claim per Pod, ordered rollout and a learning Postgres on kind.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on three-node kind v0.33.0 (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2), postgres:18-alpine, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Use a StatefulSet when each replica needs its own name and its own disk. Create the headless Service, keep claims on scale down, and back up the data.

boards.title: What a StatefulSet keeps stable
boards.hint: from the recap and the cheat sheet

rows.name: Pod names
rows.role: `web-0`, `web-1`, and so on. The set name plus the ordinal.

rows.name: volumeClaimTemplates
rows.role: One claim per Pod. Claims are named `www-web-0` and so on.

rows.name: OrderedReady
rows.role: Pods start in ordinal order and stop in reverse. One unready Pod blocks every higher ordinal.

rows.name: Parallel
rows.role: Starts them together and keeps the identities.

rows.name: partition
rows.role: Only ordinals at or above this number update.

rows.name: Claim retention
rows.role: Claims survive scale-down and deletion by default. Both policies default to Retain.

steps.title: The learning Postgres
steps.hint: what the lesson says this is, and is not

items.what: The lesson tested `postgres:18-alpine`. Postgres 18 mounts at `/var/lib/postgresql`. Versions 17 and older use `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
With OrderedReady, `web-0` becomes Ready before `web-1` is created. A 403 from a readiness probe left `web-0` unready for three minutes and `web-1` was never created.
Scale-down stops the highest ordinal first and, by default, leaves its claim. List PVCs before you reuse a StatefulSet name.
Running a database this way works for learning. The lesson says production needs replication, backups and tested restores, which later episodes cover.

homework.intro: Use the three-node kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace `k8s-from-zero`. The lesson's cluster is `k8s-ep13`. The database in the lab is for learning. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What three things does a StatefulSet give each Pod?
exercises.a: A stable name, a DNS record through a headless Service, and its own claim.

exercises.q: In what order do Pods start and stop under the default policy?
exercises.a: They start in ordinal order and stop in reverse. A Pod that is never Ready stops the line, unless you set `podManagementPolicy: Parallel`.

exercises.q: What happens to claims on scale-down and on delete, by default?
exercises.a: They survive. Both `whenDeleted` and `whenScaled` default to Retain. Set them to Delete when you want the claims removed.

exercises.q: Why can Pods fail to find each other by name even when they are Running?
exercises.a: The headless Service is missing, its name differs from `serviceName`, or its selector does not match. Check `kubectl get svc` for `CLUSTER-IP None` and compare names.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: The first version of `web-sts.yaml` probed `/` with httpGet, and the empty claim hid nginx's default page. What status code came back, and which Pods were created?
exercises.a: 403. `web-0` sat at `0/1` for three minutes. `web-1` was never created, because OrderedReady blocks every higher ordinal.

exercises.q: You change the claim template from 1Gi to 2Gi and apply again. What does the API say?
exercises.a: `spec.volumeClaimTemplates: ... field is immutable`. Grow existing claims directly if the class allows expansion, or create a new StatefulSet.

exercises.q: You revert a bad template and the rollout stays stuck. What does the lesson say to delete?
exercises.a: The Pod that was running the bad version, so the controller can recreate it. The docs call this a known issue with OrderedReady.
